headline: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee
meeting.summary: The committee discussed Bill 133, which would expand where houseless people can stay in vehicles; no vote was taken.
meeting.recap: The committee discussed Bill 133 (2026), which changes Maui County Code Chapter 10.76 on parking lots.[[0:07:14]] The chair said a 2022 law created a pilot project letting houseless people stay in their vehicles at certain county parking lots.[[0:08:44]] The bill would expand which county properties can be used and lower barriers to joining.[[0:09:53]] No vote was taken because this was a Rule 7B discussion only.[[0:10:20]] Possible changes will be weighed before second and final reading on Friday.[[0:10:29]] A county lawyer said administrative rules (written procedures) take time and cannot be ready before the pilot programs start.[[0:20:44]] One testifier asked the County to consider county parks, which already have toilets and water.[[0:25:03]] A Hawaiʻi Public Housing Authority board member said the bill removes transparency.[[0:35:04]] She asked the Council to slow down and include the people who will use the program.[[0:38:01]] Another testifier asked about liability if insurance and safety checks are waived.[[0:43:15]]
decided: The chair designated the administration staff present as resource personnel under Rule 18A, without objection.
meeting.next: A county lawyer said the Council will have to re-examine the pilot project within 12 months. A county lawyer said her office would be happy to work on draft rules as the pilot project moves forward.

moments.q: Chair explains no legislative action today
Testifier asks the Council to slow down

trackerIssues.title: Safe parking sites for people living in cars

boards.name: Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

issues.oneLine: A bill would expand where people living in vehicles can stay on county property and remove some entry requirements.
issues.why: The chair said there is an urgent need to address houselessness while keeping the public safe.
issues.next: Possible amendments are to be considered before second and final reading on Friday.
issues.brief: A county lawyer said the bill would allow other county-owned or managed parcels to be used, not just parking lots.[[#1]] The director said the temporary site would check people's ties to Maui County using a homeless data system and police records.[[#2]] The director said removing the old rules language is enough, without writing a separate exemption.[[#3]] A testifier said he met a woman with three small children living in a vehicle.[[#4]]
